title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) - DSM-5-TR Full Criteria and Evidence Base
content:
A. A persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development, as characterized by (1) and/or (2):
1. Inattention: Six (or more) of the following symptoms have persisted for at least 6 months to a degree that is inconsistent with developmental level and that negatively impacts directly on social and academic/occupational activities: a. Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes... b. Often has difficulty sustaining attention... c. Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly... d. Often does not follow through on instructions... e. Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities... f. Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort... g. Often loses things necessary for tasks/activities... h. Is often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli... i. Is often forgetful in daily activities.
2. Hyperactivity and Impulsivity: Six (or more) of: a. Often fidgets... b. Often leaves seat... c. Often runs about or climbs... d. Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly... e. Is often "on the go"... f. Often talks excessively... g. Often blurts out answers... h. Often has difficulty waiting turn... i. Often interrupts or intrudes...

B. Several inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive symptoms were present prior to age 12 years.
C. Several inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive symptoms are present in two or more settings (e.g., at home, school or work; with friends or relatives; in other activities).
D. There is clear evidence that the symptoms interfere with, or reduce the quality of, social, academic, or occupational functioning.
E. The symptoms do not occur exclusively during the course of schizophrenia or another psychotic disorder and are not better explained by another mental disorder (e.g., mood disorder, anxiety disorder, dissociative disorder, personality disorder, substance intoxication or withdrawal).

Specifiers: Combined presentation, Predominantly inattentive, Predominantly hyperactive/impulsive. In partial remission. Severity: Mild, Moderate, Severe.

Differential Diagnosis: Normal developmental variation, Oppositional Defiant Disorder, Conduct Disorder, Learning Disorders, Intellectual Disability, Autism Spectrum, Mood Disorders, Anxiety Disorders, PTSD, Substance Use, Sleep Disorders, Medical (thyroid, lead, etc.).

Research Evidence Base (2024-2026): Multimodal treatment: Stimulants (methylphenidate, amphetamines) first-line for core symptoms (effect size 0.8-1.0); atomoxetine, guanfacine, viloxazine alternatives. CBT for adults + organizational skills training. 2025: Digital therapeutics (e.g., EndeavorRx game) FDA-cleared for pediatric ADHD. Voice studies: Hyperactive speech (rapid rate, high arousal, variable dominance), inattention linked to topic drift and prosodic flattening. Continuous performance + voice biomarkers improve diagnostic specificity.

Vocal/Behavioral State Vector (BSV) Relevance: High Arousal (fidgeting, excessive talking), variable Valence, High Dominance (impulsivity, interrupting). Inattentive subtype: Lower arousal, mind-wandering prosody (pauses, pitch variability drops).
